card.name: Toxic effects at stated doses
card.fires_on: Words right before a dose or level is given in a toxicity setting, mostly "at" after toxic, "even" or "reported". Also "doses" after toxic and "LD" before 50.

modes.label: "at" before a dose
modes.description: The word "at" after a harm term, leading into doses or levels.
modes.example: Acute toxic reactions in humans have been reported<< at>> doses as low as 100

modes.label: Toxic dose terms
modes.description: The word doses itself, or the start of LD50, in poisoning text.
modes.example: Studies in animals indicate that toxic<< doses>> are associated with respiratory failure and tach

modes.label: Inside the word doses
modes.description: The ending of the capitalised word DOSES in a heading about toxic versus therapeutic amounts.
modes.example: THE RANGE BETWEEN THERAPEUTIC AND TOXIC DO<<SES>> IS NARROW.

card.writes: It pushes the model to write dose or doses as the next word.
card.plain: It fires when the text is about to name the amount at which something becomes toxic.
